case_title: Ohan Singh v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: property dispute within the victim's family; the co-accused included the victim's brother. The appellant's own relationship to the victim is not otherwise stated.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148, s.149, s.323, s.506, s.452, s.302 (charged); conviction finally under IPC s.304 Part II
evidence_type: Dying declaration; medical evidence (doctor's endorsement, medico-legal report); eyewitness testimony of injured persons; recovery of weapons
aggravating_circumstances: Very strong blow to the victim's head with an iron rod, which proved fatal; accused went to the house equipped with lathis and an iron rod; injuries to the victim's wife and daughter
mitigating_circumstances: Single blow; no intention to kill; family property dispute
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.148, 149, 323, 506, 452 and 302; sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 2000 under s.302, with other sentences for the remaining offences
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part II (culpable homicide not amounting to murder)
neutral_facts: The victim had a dispute with his brother over a residential house. On the day of the incident, the victim, his wife and his daughters were at home. A group of accused persons, including the victim's brother and other family members, entered the house and attacked the victim and his family. One accused was holding an iron rod and struck the victim a blow on the head and left ear. Other accused beat the victim with lathis on his back, hips and other parts of the body, and the victim's wife and daughter were also injured with lathi blows. The accused then ran away, threatening to kill the family on the next opportunity. The injured were taken to a government hospital. The attending doctor was asked whether the victim was fit to make a statement and certified that he was. A police head constable then recorded the victim's statement, which the doctor endorsed after confirming its accuracy and which the victim's children also signed. The statement described the role of each accused and formed the basis of the first information report. The medico-legal examination recorded multiple lacerated wounds, contusions and abrasions, including a lacerated wound on the right side of the head. The victim's condition later worsened and he was transferred to another hospital, where he died about a week after the incident. The post-mortem was conducted by a doctor. Investigators recovered lathis and dandas following disclosure statements by accused persons. At trial, the victim's wife and daughter did not support the prosecution account, and the victim's son and daughter were not examined as witnesses.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a head injury; multiple lacerations, contusions and abrasions to the victim; injuries to the victim's wife and daughter
premeditation_planning: Not found. The court held there was no evidence the accused went to the house intending to kill.
motive: Property dispute between the victim and his brother (accepted by the court as a family property dispute)
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration recorded by the police head constable after the doctor's fitness endorsement; the doctor's testimony and medico-legal report; injured witnesses' accounts
witness_credibility: The doctor (PW-1) and the dying declaration were found credible and corroborated. The hostility of the wife (PW-3) and daughter (PW-4) did not defeat the prosecution case.
post_offence_conduct: Declared a proclaimed offender; taken into custody on 18.12.1997
custody_duration: Taken into custody on 18.12.1997; total duration not stated
trial_duration: offence: 15.07.1997; trial judgment: 17.05.1999; High Court: 30.04.2008; Supreme Court: 22.07.2010
legal_representation: Appellant: Biswajit Swain (for Rajesh Prasad Singh); State: B.S. Mor (for T.V. George)
investigation_status: FIR registered under ss.148, 452, 323, 506 r/w s.149 IPC; case converted to s.302 after death; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Dying declaration recorded by a Head Constable rather than a Magistrate or doctor; the FIR sections could not be investigated by a Head Constable (undisputed). The court found no legal infirmity in admissibility.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced (life imprisonment under s.302). High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld. Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; s.302 altered to s.304 Part II with 10 years RI and fine of Rs. 20,000.
prosecution_argument: Not separately recorded in the judgment. The State supported the conviction, relying on the admissibility and reliability of the dying declaration and the medical evidence.
defence_argument: Dying declaration recorded by Head Constable was unreliable and should have been recorded by a Magistrate; sons and daughter not examined and findings perverse; alternatively conviction should be under s.304 Part II
legal_principle_applied: Admissibility of dying declaration under s.32(1) Evidence Act, not dependent on who records it; hostile witnesses do not by themselves defeat the prosecution; conviction for murder altered to culpable homicide where intention/knowledge to cause death is not established
precedent_relied_upon: Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab (1979) 4 SCC 332 (relied on); Cherlopalli Cheliminabi Sahed v. State of A.P. (2003) 2 SCC 571 and Kanti Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2004) 10 SCC 113 (distinguished); State (Delhi Administration) v. Laxman Kumar (1985) 4 SCC 476 (referred); Jagriti Devi v. State of H.P. (2009) 14 SCC 771 and Gurmukh Singh v. State of Haryana (2009) 15 SCC 635 (referred)
sentencing_rationale: Court found no intention to kill or knowledge that the blow was likely to cause death, so the offence was altered to s.304 Part II
judicial_mitigating_factors: Single blow; no intention to kill; family property dispute
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused went to the house equipped with lathis and an iron rod; a very strong blow to the head with the iron rod proved fatal
other_sentence_order: Default sentence of six months rigorous imprisonment for non-payment of fine
